entry.title: Revisiting Privacy Risks in Quantized Deep Neural Networks
entry.summary:
Model quantization has become a fundamental technique for enabling the efficient deployment of large-scale deep neural networks (DNNs) in data-intensive applications by reducing model size. Despite its widespread adoption, the impact of quantization on training data privacy --- particularly vulnerability to membership inference attacks (MIAs) --- remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive empirical study of privacy risks in quantized DNNs, evaluating eight state-of-the-art MIA attacks across six representative quantization methods.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec #neuroscience

entry.title: Analyzing Compiler-induced Constant-time Violations with Compiler at Scale. The constant-time programming policy is a de facto standard for cryptographic libraries to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
entry.summary:
The constant-time programming policy is a de facto standard for cryptographic libraries to prevent timing side-channel attacks. However, compiler optimizations may break constant-time source code during compilation. Systematically preventing this requires understanding where a violation arises, how it is introduced, and which compiler configurations are problematic.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: ReedWeave: Faster Reed-Solomon Polynomial Commitments from Interleaving and Folding
entry.summary:
Polynomial commitment schemes (PCSs) allow a prover to commit to a polynomial and later prove its evaluations succinctly. Among hash-based constructions, FRI (Ben-Sasson et al., ICALP 2018) and its follow-up works achieve polylogarithmic proofs by recursively ``folding'' Reed-Solomon (RS) codes. However, their concrete evaluation costs remain relatively high, as the first few folding rounds operate on the largest codewords and dominate the prover work.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust

entry.title: RDK-CKKS: A Framework for Rigorous Error Analysis of CKKS Computation. The CKKS scheme allows approximate arithmetic on encrypted data, and has found widespread use in privacy-preserving computation.
entry.summary:
The CKKS scheme allows approximate arithmetic on encrypted data, and has found widespread use in privacy-preserving computation. A rigorous control of its homomorphic error is critical for both precision and security guarantees. In particular, in some settings such as IND-CPA^D or threshold settings, the latter computation error should be hidden at the time of decryption.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Knowledge Soundness of Polynomial Commitments in the Algebraic Group Model Does Not Guarantee Extractability
entry.summary:
The Algebraic Group Model (AGM) has become a standard framework for analyzing the knowledge soundness of group-based polynomial commitment schemes. In this work, we formally establish inherent limitations of this methodology. For many PCSs analyzed in the AGM, the algebraic explanation directly determines a polynomial and any required randomness that together reproduce the commitment.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: More Efficient Secret-Shared Joins with Multiplicity via Oblivious Sort Expansion
entry.summary:
Secret-shared SQL-style join is a fundamental building block in secure collaborative data analysis. In practice, join operations frequently involve duplicate keys, giving rise to one-to-many (Join-OM) and many-to-many (Join-MM) relationships. Supporting such joins requires obliviously materializing all matching row pairs.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #databases
